intro.text: Enormous greatshells that roam the chasms of the Shattered Plains, hunted for the huge gemhearts they carry. The Alethi call them Roshar's deadliest predators.

description.text: Ancient pictures of Voidbringers were often based on chasmfiends, but Jasnah thinks the artists, living long after the Desolations, simply drew the most terrifying creature they knew.
Alethi sayings include "Even a chasmfiend stops fighting when it's been decapitated" and "trying to choose which claw of the chasmfiend would crush you".
On the Shattered Plains a chasmfiend nests in the chasms, hunting and scavenging, until one night it climbs onto a plateau and forms a rock-coloured chrysalis that awaits a highstorm.

A chasmfiend is armoured in dark violet carapace that can shrug off a hail of arrows; its blood is purple. It has eighteen legs: four huge clawed foreclaws on broad shoulders for smashing and slicing, and fourteen smaller limbs that can move it very fast.
Like every greatshell, a chasmfiend grows a gemheart, always an emerald and especially large. When it dies, the mandras that help bear its weight leave its body like tongues of smoke.

items.text: Before the war chasmfiends were almost legendary, and killing one was extremely rare; even Gavilar never managed it.

During the war listeners and humans hunted chasmfiends for their gemhearts, usually by finding a chrysalis, when the beast is most vulnerable, and breaking it open with mallets and Shardblades. The biggest danger was other armies after the same chrysalis.
Adult chasmfiends that strayed into a highprince's territory were sometimes lured up onto a plateau with hog carcasses and blood and fought there.
The Alethi commonly believed the listeners worshipped chasmfiends as gods, a misunderstanding by early explorers that Shallan came to doubt.
Over fifteen were killed each month, and by the war's last years their numbers were dwindling. Some proposed fewer hunts or even breeding them in captivity.
After Urithiru's rediscovery its early population depended on gemhearts from plateau runs, but as chasmfiends dwindled the armies relied more on farming and lumber from the warcamps.
Gemhearts drove Alethkar's wartime economy: one could fund a highprince's war for months, and large ones were vital for Soulcasting. Much of the royal emerald reserve likely came from them.
The listeners used gemhearts not as money but as an energy source to grow food on the barren plains.
Chasmfiends share mental images and impressions with one another and with singers.
They test strength by challenging rivals or stealing prey; a weaker animal usually yields without a deadly fight.
During highstorms, they form protective rings around smaller chasmfiends and listener allies.
Young chasmfiends pupate repeatedly as they grow. The tone of the Well of Control draws them to the Shattered Plains for their final pupation.
The first humans to kill a chasmfiend convinced the others that humans and listeners were rivals rather than insignificant smaller creatures.
Discovering that those rivals were killing their pupating young led the chasmfiends to regard them as dominant.
Chasmfiends allied with Thude's listeners, trading protection and shared food for grooming.
Five accompanied Venli's party toward Narak and helped the listeners traverse the chasms.
They carried listeners into the second battle at Narak and helped their deception.
They remained with the listeners after their allies made a truce with the humans.
